patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a compact header with a small square icon containing horizontal lines in the top-right, a conventional hamburger/menu trigger, while full navigation links are not visible inline.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close a navigation panel or overlay containing the site links. The trigger should reflect open/closed state and likely hide body scroll while the menu is open.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as a full-screen overlay, slide-in drawer, or dropdown panel.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches place branding/navigation at the very top in a persistent header-like band, while the rest of the page is long-form content below; this strongly implies the header remains available during scrolling.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Header/navigation should remain fixed or become fixed on scroll so branding and navigation stay accessible while reading the page content.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly indicate whether the header is always fixed or only becomes sticky after scrolling.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The page composition in both sketches is content-heavy and vertically scrollable, especially the mobile sketch with a very long article-like body, which commonly implies a return-to-top affordance even if not explicitly drawn.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A back-to-top control would typically appear after the user scrolls down and smoothly return focus/scroll position to the top when activated.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit button is drawn in either sketch, so this is inferred from the long-scroll layout rather than directly depicted.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a relatively simple informational page with limited JavaScript needs: the main cross-viewport behavior is a persistent top navigation/header, while the clearest mobile-specific interaction is a hamburger-triggered navigation menu. No forms, tabs, accordions, modals, dropdown submenus, or dynamic loading controls are visibly suggested by the drawings. The only additional inferred enhancement is a scroll-to-top affordance due to the unusually long reading layout, but that remains speculative because it is not explicitly sketched.
